message: No detected untrusted source handling: Data is pulled via `dvc pull` and read from local CSV paths without any checksum verification, signature validation, or authenticated source pinning.
No detected label flipping detection: The code reads the CSV and directly uses labels for training without any validation of label values, distribution checks, or label-noise detection tools.
No detected data poisoning defenses: There are no outlier detection, statistical anomaly checks, or suspicious input filtering steps applied to the training data before model fitting.

No detected model integrity verification: The model is loaded with joblib.load() in both main.py (line 12) and training.py without any hash check, signature verification, or pinned revision; it simply loads the file from a relative path with no integrity controls.
No detected label distribution validation: The code performs no class balance check, expected-label-set validation, or anomaly detection on labels before training begins.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: There is no trigger detection, activation analysis, or gradient anomaly detection anywhere in the training pipeline.
No detected differential privacy: The code uses a standard scikit-learn RandomForestClassifier with no differential privacy library (Opacus, TF Privacy, DP-SGD, etc.) applied.
No detected adversarial robustness testing: No adversarial robustness libraries (Foolbox, ART, FGSM/PGD) or any stress-test routines are present anywhere in the code.

No detected metric tampering protection: The inference function evaluates on the full dataset without a properly isolated, held-out test set, there is no signed/hashed evaluation data, and the train/test split in train_test_model uses a random (unseeded) split whose results are never stored or cross-checked, providing no protection against
No detected output bounds checks: The inference path returns pred[0] directly from model.predict() with no NaN checks, probability bounds validation, or sanity checks on the output.
No detected prompt injection defenses: This is a tabular classification model (RandomForestClassifier), not an LLM, so prompt-injection defenses are not applicable and none are implemented.
